kurz: Which economic data are published when, what they measure, how accurate they are and why the market reacts only to the deviation from expectations.

bloecke.md:
An economic figure moves prices when it turns out differently from what was expected. Whether it is good or bad in itself plays no role. The benchmark is the economists' consensus, not the previous month's value. A US inflation rate of 3.4% triggers nothing if 3.4% is already priced in. If, on the other hand, 3.4% is expected and 3.7% is reported, the bond market moves within seconds. Every indicator therefore comes with two figures: the reported value and the expectation. Investors who only know the value are regularly surprised when good news is followed by falling prices.

September 2026 provides a textbook example. Sentiment data are mixed, and the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index stood at 47.8 points in September according to preliminary figures, close to its record low. Nevertheless, the Fed raised its target range to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September. The reason is the oil price: between 9 and 15 September, Brent rose from $109.51 to $130.80 per barrel. A supply shock drives prices up and output down. The two goals of the central bank's mandate then call for opposite responses, and no decision is right for both goals.

## Surveys and measurements

Soft data are based on surveys, such as the PMI, [[ifo Business Climate Index|ifo]], ZEW and consumer confidence. They are available early, often while the month is still under way, and measure assessments. Hard data are counted quantities such as production, sales, employment and gross domestic product. They are more reliable and are published weeks to months later.

Purchasing managers' indices are [[Diffusion index|diffusion indices]]. Respondents are asked whether something has become better, stayed the same or become worse, not by how much it has changed. The share of improvements plus half of the unchanged responses gives a value around the threshold of 50. A manufacturing PMI of 54.3 therefore means that more firms report an increase than a decrease. It does not show how large the increase is. This is why Germany can have a manufacturing PMI of 54.3 in August 2026, the highest since May 2022, and at the same time industrial production that was 1.8% below the previous year in July according to revised figures, and just over 3% below excluding energy and construction. Both figures are correct; they simply measure different things.

bloecke.unter: Values above 50 indicate growth in the respective sector, values below it contraction. The only value below the threshold is German construction, even though it rose from 42.1 to 48.7.

bloecke.md:
## German sentiment indicators

For the **ifo Business Climate**, around 9,000 companies are surveyed every month about their current situation and their expectations for the next six months. The two are combined into the index, based on 2015 = 100. In August 2026 it stood at 88.8, after 86.7 in July. For the **ZEW Economic Sentiment**, financial market experts are surveyed rather than companies. Instead of an index, the result is a balance: the share of optimists minus the share of pessimists, which can theoretically lie between -100 and +100. In September 2026 it stood at +34.7 points, well above its long-term average of roughly 21 points. The **GfK/NIM Consumer Climate** measures household sentiment and stood at -26.6 in September, after -29.4. Its sub-components are more revealing than the overall value. Income expectations rose markedly to +1.7, the propensity to buy remained at -9.8, and the propensity to save is high at 15.5. Households therefore expect more money but do not want to spend it.

ifo is an index with a base of 100, ZEW a balance from -100 to +100, GfK a points score of its own. A chart that shows all three without normalisation is therefore meaningless. The same applies outside Germany. The University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index (47.8 in September 2026, preliminary) and the Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (89.4 in August) measure similar things with different samples, questions and scales. The gap between the two values results from the methodology and contains no information about the situation.

## The US employment report

The US employment report is usually published on the first Friday of the month at 14:30 German time and is based on two separate surveys. The **nonfarm payrolls** come from the establishment survey and count jobs. In August 2026 the figure was +162,000 according to the first release (revised to +133,000 in the following report of 2 October), a lot compared with the twelve-month average of only 31,000. The **unemployment rate** comes from the household survey and stood at 4.1%, which corresponds to around 7.0 million unemployed people. The two figures can move in opposite directions without either of them being wrong.

The rate on its own is misleading, because it falls when people find work and also when they give up looking. This is why the [[Labour force participation rate|labour force participation rate]] is part of the analysis. It stood at 61.6% in August 2026 and has fallen by 0.5 percentage points since January. The favourable unemployment rate is therefore partly due to people withdrawing from the labour market. The fastest data available are the weekly initial claims for unemployment benefits. They are published every Thursday with a lag of only a few days and fluctuate accordingly.

bloecke.titel: Weekly US initial claims for unemployment benefits
bloecke.unter: In thousands, seasonally adjusted. The fall from 206,000 to 196,000 looks like a turnaround but is within the usual weekly fluctuation. The market therefore usually looks at the four-week average, here 203,250.

bloecke.formel: Sahm indicator = Ø(unemployment rate over the last 3 months) − lowest value of this average over the last 12 months
bloecke.erklaerung: The Sahm rule sums up the labour market in a single number. At +0.50 percentage points or more, the indicator is considered triggered. It measures how quickly unemployment is rising, not its level. Experience shows that when the labour market deteriorates, it does so quickly.
variablen: three-month moving average of the US unemployment rate
the minimum of this three-month average over the preceding twelve months
bloecke.beispiel: In August 2026 the value was -0.07 percentage points (FRED series SAHMREALTIME). The current average is therefore lower than the twelve-month minimum, and there is no signal.

bloecke.md: Claudia Sahm designed her rule as a real-time description, not as a forecasting model. It was meant to recognise whether a recession was already under way, so that relief payments could start quickly. In 2024 it was triggered without a recession following. One reason was that the unemployment rate was then rising partly because of immigration into the labour market, not only because of layoffs. Rules based on around a dozen observed US recessions are rules of thumb with a very small sample. This applies to the Sahm rule as much as to the yield curve.

## Different measures of inflation

Every inflation figure must state which rate is meant. In August 2026, the US consumer price index (CPI) stood at 3.4%, and the US core rate excluding food and energy at 2.4%. For the CPI, the gap shows that the price surge comes almost entirely from energy (+16.3% year on year) and has not yet become broadly entrenched in the economy. However, the Fed measures its 2% target neither by the CPI nor by its core rate. What counts for the Fed is the personal consumption expenditures price index (PCE). It uses different weights and takes into account that households switch to other goods when prices jump. In August 2026, according to the release of 30 September, it stood at 3.4%, around 1.4 points above the target. **Core PCE** excluding food and energy, which the Fed monitors as a measure of the underlying trend, stood at 3.0%. By this measure, price pressure is clearly elevated even excluding food and energy. Here, the word inflation covers four figures, each with a different message.

In Germany, the same distinction applies under different names. Destatis publishes the national consumer price index (CPI, 2.9% in August 2026, driven by energy at +10.5%, while food rose by only +0.1%). The ECB, by contrast, is guided by the harmonised HICP for the euro area, which stood at around 3.2% in August. For your own purchasing power, the headline rate is what counts. The targets of the Fed and the ECB also refer to the headline rate; they use the core rate as an indication of the underlying trend. The producer price index (PPI) tends to lead the consumer price index, because costs are passed on with a delay, although incompletely and with a varying lag. It therefore provides a pointer, but not a fixed formula.

bloecke.unter: Annual rates in August 2026; the BEA published the two PCE figures on 30 September 2026. The Fed is guided by the headline PCE index, the ECB by the HICP.

bloecke.titel: The CPI as a legal reference
bloecke.md: The German consumer price index has direct legal consequences. With an index-linked rent (Indexmiete) under Section 557b BGB (Civil Code), the rent is linked to the CPI determined by the Federal Statistical Office, and it must remain unchanged for at least one year at a time. For company pensions, Section 16(1) BetrAVG (Occupational Pensions Act) requires the employer to carry out an adjustment review every three years. Under Section 16(2) BetrAVG, the obligation is deemed to be fulfilled if the adjustment at least matches the rise in the CPI. Under Section 68 SGB VI (Social Code Book VI, pension insurance), the statutory pension, by contrast, essentially follows wage growth rather than prices. In a year with an energy price surge and weak wage growth, this makes a noticeable difference. The basic rate of interest (Basiszinssatz) under Section 247 BGB is based on the ECB's interest rate level, changes on 1 January and 1 July, and has stood at 1.52% since 1 July 2026. This gives the default interest rates under Section 288 BGB: 6.52% for consumers (a mark-up of 5 points) and 10.52% in commercial transactions not involving consumers (9 points).

## Retail, new orders and construction

US retail sales rose by 1.2% on the previous month in August 2026. This was the strongest increase in five months, with July having previously been revised to -0.5%. Two points are important for putting this into context. First, the sales figures are **nominal**, and petrol stations alone grew by 3.1%, which reflects higher prices, not a larger volume. Second, the market watches the control group, which excludes cars, petrol, building materials and food services, because only this group feeds into the consumption component of GDP in an approximately undistorted way. It rose by 1.4%.

German industrial new orders rose by 2.5% in July according to the first release (3.2% after revision), the third month in a row. Almost the entire increase came from large orders in shipbuilding, rail vehicle construction and aircraft construction (+126.4%), while orders for motor vehicles fell by 12.5%. Destatis therefore also publishes the series excluding large orders. Without this adjustment, a single ship order could look like a turnaround. Construction is the most interest-sensitive sector and therefore a classic leading indicator. US housing starts were at an annualised 1.275 million units in August 2026, 2.6% below the previous month and at their lowest level since May 2026.

US retail sales were reported at a nominal +1.2% on the previous month for August 2026. The US CPI rose by +0.4% in the same month.

- Rough approximation: 1.2 − 0.4 = around 0.8% real growth.
- Exact calculation: 1.012 / 1.004 − 1 = 0.00797, that is, +0.80%.
- One third of the nominal increase was therefore due to higher prices.

The calculation is an approximation, because the CPI basket of goods and the retail sales basket are not identical. It is sufficient for the order of magnitude. It shows what the headline leaves open, namely whether consumers bought more or merely paid more.

bloecke.md:
## Composite index and yield curve

The Conference Board's Leading Economic Index offers a summary of many individual releases. It combines ten leading indicators, including hours worked in manufacturing, initial claims, new orders, building permits, share prices, credit conditions, the interest rate spread and consumer expectations, and aims to provide a lead of around seven months. In August 2026 it stood at 99.5 (2016 = 100), 0.1% below the previous month. This was the first decline since March; four of the ten components fell. It did not trigger a recession signal, and the accompanying Coincident Index rose to 114.9.

The yield curve is the best-known single leading indicator. Every US recession since 1955 was preceded by an inversion, with a lead of six to twenty-four months. There were two false alarms: in 1966, and with the long inversion from 2022 to 2024, which was not followed by a recession within two years. On 18 September 2026, the spread between ten-year and two-year US government bonds was +0.25 percentage points, and the ten-year versus three-month spread preferred by the New York Fed was +0.87. Both values are positive and therefore give no signal. Since the lead can vary between six months and two years, an inversion does not indicate a time to sell. It describes a general risk situation.

PMI, ifo and the yield curve are public, and their message is reflected in prices within minutes. Investors who reallocate in response pay the spread and order fees, and, when they realise gains in their portfolio, flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) as well, all for information that the market has already processed. In addition, there is revision risk, because the decision is based on a first estimate that is corrected later. Indicators help you understand the situation and calibrate your own expectations. They are not suitable for getting in and out of the market.

1. Compare the value with the expectation. Without a comparison with the consensus, the absolute value says nothing about the market reaction.
2. Clarify the type of figure: soft or hard, nominal or real, previous month or previous year, annualised or not. A US GDP figure of +1.5% is annualised and corresponds to around +0.37% on the previous quarter, not 7.5 times the German flash estimate of +0.2%.
3. Distinguish between the first estimate and the revised value. The first figure is an estimate, not yet a measured value.

US payrolls are aligned every year with the more complete data reported to the unemployment insurance system. In recent years, this benchmark revision has on several occasions corrected the figures down by several hundred thousand jobs. German GDP goes through a flash estimate, a second estimate, detailed results and, later, comprehensive revisions. For the second quarter of 2026, the flash estimate of 30 July gave +0.2% on the previous quarter, and the detailed results of 25 August already +0.3%. In any headline, a tenth of a point makes the difference between “stagnation” and “tentative growth”. To assess the economy, you should therefore take series from a database (Bundesbank time series, Destatis, FRED) rather than from old press releases. The database shows the revised series, the press release only the figures as they stood at the time.

All the series mentioned are freely accessible, from Destatis and the Federal Employment Agency, Eurostat and the ECB, the BLS, BEA, Fed and Conference Board, and also from FRED as a central collection point with series you can subscribe to. Four dates a month are enough: PMI at the start of the month, the US labour market on the first Friday, US CPI in the middle of the month and ifo at the end of the month. All other data are for monitoring and are not a basis for decisions.

mitnehmen: Prices react to a figure's deviation from the consensus, not to its absolute value.
Surveys are published early and measure sentiment, counted data are published late and measure quantities; in Germany, the two diverge markedly in 2026.
A diffusion index such as the PMI measures the breadth of a change, not its strength; its threshold is 50, not zero.
CPI, core rate, PCE, core PCE and HICP give different inflation rates for the same period; the Fed's target refers to the headline PCE index, the ECB's to the HICP.
First estimates are revised and individual months fluctuate strongly, so the economy is best judged by averages and series, not by headlines.

begriffe.text: Index form that counts only the direction of changes and thus measures the breadth of a movement, not its strength. It is calculated as the share of companies reporting an improvement plus half of those reporting no change. Values above 50 mean growth, values below it contraction.

Recession indicator that is considered triggered when the three-month average of the US unemployment rate is 0.50 percentage points or more above its twelve-month low. Claudia Sahm designed it as a real-time description, not as a forecast; in 2024 it gave a false alarm.

Personal consumption expenditures price index excluding food and energy, published by the US agency BEA. It takes substitution between goods into account. The Fed's 2% target refers to the headline PCE index, not to the consumer price index CPI; the Fed uses core PCE as a measure of the underlying trend.

Share of the reference population that is working or actively looking for work; in US statistics, the reference population is all civilians aged 16 and over who do not live in institutions, with no upper age limit. When it falls, the unemployment rate can fall even though no additional people have been employed. This makes it indispensable when reading labour market data.

First publication of an official statistic, estimated on an incomplete data basis, for example of gross domestic product around 30 days after the end of the quarter. It is later corrected by the second estimate, detailed results and comprehensive revisions.
